title: Operational Onboarding and Authorization Playbook (2025)
body:
> **Archived 2026-02-15:** this page is superseded by "Operational Onboarding and Authorization Playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Overview
--------
This playbook pulls together Redwood's company-wide operational policies: onboarding people and services, access and permissions, change authorization, data lifecycle, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel approvals. It is meant as one practical reference for managers, security, legal, finance, and engineering.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who need system access or handle company data. These procedures are mandatory unless an approved exception is logged in Risk and Exceptions.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege by default.
- Separation of duties for sensitive approvals.
- Time-boxed, auditable changes.
- Risk-based procurement and vendor due diligence.
- Named owners and SLAs for operational requests.

1) Access & Permissions
----------------------
All access requests, role assignments, and privileged elevation go through the central flow to keep IAM clean and auditable.

Owner: Identity and Access team (eng-infra) | Request queue: OPS-AUTH
SLA: Standard role requests: 72 business hours. Privileged (root/keyholder) access: 5 business days with approved justification. Emergency access: documented within 24 hours after the event.

Process (standard requests):
1. Submit the request in OPS-AUTH with reason, duration, and target resource (tag: AUTH-REQ-<team>).
2. Manager approves first.
3. System owner approves second for non-privileged roles; privileged roles also require Security review.
4. Identity team applies the RBAC change and records the grant on the ticket.
5. Grants are time-limited where possible; automation sends an expiry reminder 7 days ahead.

Privileged Access Controls:
- Multi-person attestation every 180 days for privileged accounts.
- MFA on all privileged logins.
- Session recording on admin consoles where supported.

Example IAM snippet:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:GetObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-artifacts/*"]}
  ]
}

2) Change Management (Governed Changes)
--------------------------------------
Infrastructure, schema, data pipeline, and product-facing changes are triaged as Standard, Normal, or Emergency.

Change Window: Tue–Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC for disruptive infra changes.
Change Advisory Board (CAB): weekly on Thursdays, 16:00 UTC. Emergency escalations go to #ops-cab on Slack.

Categories and approvals:
- Standard (low-risk, pre-authorized): self-serve for routine library upgrades and small config tweaks. Approver: Team lead.
- Normal: rolling deploys, infra changes affecting <10% of traffic. Approver: Service owner + SRE reviewer via CAB.
- Emergency (P1/P2 incidents): post-change review within 48 hours; must include a rollback plan.

Normal change checklist:
- Impact analysis and rollback plan (template: CHANGE-IMPACT-2025).
- Test plan and validation criteria.
- Monitoring/alerting updates.
- Stakeholder notification list.

3) Data Management and Retention
--------------------------------
Classification levels:
- Public: external distribution OK. Retention: as needed.
- Internal: non-sensitive operational data. Retention: 3 years (default).
- Restricted: personal, customer-identifying, or regulated data. Retention: 7 years or per contract.
- Confidential: legal, M&A, security artifacts. Retention: 10 years or per legal hold.

Handling:
- Restricted and Confidential data encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys.
- Access to Restricted+ data is logged; PII-producing queries need approval.
- Backups follow the same classification and appear in the Data Inventory.

Deletion and eDiscovery:
- Data owners run quarterly purges and report compliance.
- Legal holds override automated deletion.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Approval thresholds (USD):
- Under $5,000: Manager approval; procurement notified via PR-INT.
- $5,000–$50,000: Procurement review + 2 approvers (Manager + Procurement Lead).
- $50,001–$250,000: Procurement + Finance Director + Vendor Risk assessment.
- >$250,000 or multi-year: Legal + VP/Head-level approval and Procurement Sourcing.

Card & expense rules:
- Use the company card where practical. Reimbursements need original receipts per the TRVL-EXP-2024 template.
- Pre-approval needed for travel or expenses expected above $1,000.
- Software and subscriptions go through procurement; shadow IT purchases face retroactive review and possible chargebacks.

Timelines:
- Standard SaaS with SOC2 docs: target 10 business days.
- Custom contracts: 20+ business days.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
----------------------------------
Minimum steps (Vendor ID: VND-ONB-2025):
1. Vendor intake form (Finance/Procurement portal).
2. Security questionnaire (SIG or Redwood Alternate) and baseline review.
3. SOC2 Type II or equivalent for services handling sensitive data, or documented compensating controls.
4. Contract + DPA review by Legal.
5. Payment terms and tax forms collected by Finance.
6. Least-privilege, time-boxed service accounts for any access.

Ongoing:
- Quarterly spend and performance review for vendors >$50k/year.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials, confirm data return/destruction, terminate integrations.

6) Travel & Business Expense Policy (summary)
--------------------------------------------
- All business travel needs manager pre-approval in Travel Portal (TP-APP); travel >$1,000 also needs Finance pre-approval.
- Emergency travel: manager approval within 24 hours after booking.

Per diem & lodging (USD):
- Domestic per diem: $60/day. International per diem: $150/day.
- Lodging cap: $300/night domestic; $450/night international; high-cost markets by pre-approval.
- Flights: economy; premium economy for flights >8 hours or approved medical/other reasons.

Submission: TRVL-EXP-2024 template within 10 business days of return; itemized receipts for items >$25.

7) Templates & Forms
--------------------
- Access request: OPS-AUTH-REQ
- Change impact: CHANGE-IMPACT-2025
- Procurement intake: PR-INT-FORM
- Vendor onboarding: VND-ONB-2025
- Travel/expense: TRVL-EXP-2024

Sample Change Impact:
- Change ID: <team>-YYYYMMDD-<seq>
- Summary, Owner, Rollback plan (steps + time to restore), Test criteria, Monitoring

8) Responsibilities & Escalation Matrix
-------------------------------------
- Requester: justification and duration.
- Manager: first-level approval and budget check.
- Procurement: vendor terms, licensing, vendor risk.
- Legal: contract and DPA review for >$50k or any data processing.
- Security: privileged access and vendor security posture.
- Identity & Access team: RBAC changes and audit records.

Escalations:
- Access SLA breach → notify Head of Eng and Security within 24 hours.
- Procurement disputes → Finance Director.

9) Exceptions and Risk Acceptance
--------------------------------
Deviations need an exception ticket in the Risk and Exceptions registry with compensating controls, stakeholders, and a sunset date. Exceptions expire after 12 months unless renewed.

10) Audit, Metrics & Reporting
-----------------------------
Quarterly Finance/Security reports: access grants and time-to-provision, emergency changes and rollback rate, vendor spend >$50k and risk scores, travel spend and per-diem variance.

KPIs:
- 90% of standard access requests within SLA.
- 100% of Restricted+ data encrypted at rest.
- 0 unresolved critical vendor findings older than 30 days.

Appendix A — AWS CLI revoke example
-----------------------------------
aws iam remove-user-from-group --user-name alice.kumar --group-name developers

Appendix B — Change rollback checklist
--------------------------------------
1. Open rollback ticket, notify CAB.
2. Stop new traffic via feature flags or routing.
3. Restore last known-good state.
4. Smoke test.
5. Monitor 60 minutes; close with postmortem if needed.

Contact
-------
operations@redwood.ai (triage) or the section owners above.
